{{Short description|Probability distribution}}
The '''Kaniadakis exponential distribution''' (or '''''κ''-exponential distribution)''' is a [[probability distribution]] arising from the maximization of the [[Kaniadakis entropy]] under appropriate constraints.  It is one example of a [[Kaniadakis distribution]]. The ''κ''-exponential is a generalization of the [[exponential distribution]] in the same way that Kaniadakis entropy is a generalization of standard [[Entropy (statistical thermodynamics)|Boltzmann–Gibbs entropy]] or [[Entropy (information theory)|Shannon entropy]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Kaniadakis |first=G. |date=2001 |title=Non-linear kinetics underlying generalized statistics |url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/S0378437101001844 |journal=Physica A: Statistical Mechanics and Its Applications |language=en |volume=296 |issue=3–4 |pages=405–425 |doi=10.1016/S0378-4371(01)00184-4|arxiv=cond-mat/0103467 |bibcode=2001PhyA..296..405K |s2cid=44275064 }}</ref> The ''κ''-exponential distribution of Type I is a particular case of the [[Kaniadakis Gamma distribution|''κ''-Gamma distribution]], whilst the ''κ''-exponential distribution of Type II is a particular case of the [[Kaniadakis Weibull distribution|''κ''-Weibull distribution]].

== Type I ==

===Probability density function===
{{Probability distribution
  | name       = ''κ''-exponential distribution of type I
  | type       = density
  | parameters = <math> 0 < \kappa < 1 </math> [[shape parameter|shape]] ([[Real number|real]]) <br /> <math> \beta> 0 </math> [[rate parameter|rate]] ([[Real number|real]])
  | support    = <math>x \in [0, \infty)</math>
  | pdf        = <math>(1 - \kappa^2) \beta \exp_\kappa(-\beta x)</math>
  | cdf        = <math>1-\Big(\sqrt{1+\kappa^2\beta^2 x^2} + \kappa^2 \beta x \Big)\exp_k({-\beta x)}</math>
  | mean       = <math>\frac{1}{\beta} \frac{1 - \kappa^2}{1 - 4\kappa^2}</math>
  | variance   = <math> \sigma_\kappa^2 =\frac{1}{\beta^2} \frac{2(1-4\kappa^2)^2 - (1 - \kappa^2)^2(1-9\kappa^2)}{(1-4\kappa^2)^2(1-9\kappa^2)}</math>
  |pdf_image=File:Kaniadakis Exponential Distribution Type I pdf.png|cdf_image=File:Kaniadakis Exponential Distribution Type I cdf.png|moments=<math> \frac{1 - \kappa^2}{\prod_{n=0}^{m+1} [1-(2n-m-1) \kappa ]} \frac{m!}{\beta^m} </math>|kurtosis=<math> \frac{ 9(1200\kappa^{14} - 6123\kappa^{12} + 562\kappa^{10} +1539 \kappa^8 - 544 \kappa^6 + 143 \kappa^4 -18\kappa^2 + 1  )}{ \beta^4 \sigma_\kappa^4 (1-\kappa^2)^{-1}(1 - 4\kappa^2)^4 (3600\kappa^8 -4369\kappa^6 + 819\kappa^4 - 51\kappa^2 + 1) }   - 3 </math>|skewness=<math> \frac{ 2 (1-\kappa^2) (144 \kappa^8+23 \kappa^6+27 \kappa^4-6 \kappa^2+1) }{ \beta^3 \sigma^3_\kappa (4 \kappa^2-1)^3 (144 \kappa^4-25 \kappa^2+1) }  </math>}}

The Kaniadakis ''κ''-exponential distribution of Type I is part of a class of [[statistical distributions]] emerging from the [[Kaniadakis statistics|Kaniadakis κ-statistics]] which exhibit power-law tails. This distribution has the following [[probability density function]]:<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal |last=Kaniadakis |first=G. |date=2021-01-01 |title=New power-law tailed distributions emerging in κ-statistics (a) |url=https://iopscience.iop.org/article/10.1209/0295-5075/133/10002 |journal=Europhysics Letters |volume=133 |issue=1 |article-number=10002 |doi=10.1209/0295-5075/133/10002 |issn=0295-5075|arxiv=2203.01743 |bibcode=2021EL....13310002K |s2cid=234144356 }}</ref>

:<math> 
f_{_{\kappa}}(x) = (1 - \kappa^2) \beta \exp_\kappa(-\beta x)
</math>

valid for <math>x \ge 0</math>, where <math>0 \leq |\kappa| < 1</math> is the entropic index associated with the [[Kaniadakis statistics|Kaniadakis entropy]] and <math>\beta > 0</math> is known as [[rate parameter]]. The [[exponential distribution]] is recovered as <math>\kappa \rightarrow 0.</math>

===Cumulative distribution function===
The [[cumulative distribution function]] of ''κ''-exponential distribution of Type I is given by

:<math>F_\kappa(x) = 1-\Big(\sqrt{1+\kappa^2\beta^2 x^2} + \kappa^2 \beta x \Big)\exp_k({-\beta x)} </math>

for <math>x \ge 0</math>. The cumulative [[exponential distribution]] is recovered in the classical limit <math>\kappa \rightarrow 0</math>.

=== Properties ===

==== Moments, expectation value and variance ====
The ''κ''-exponential distribution of type I has moment of order <math>m \in \mathbb{N}</math> given by<ref name=":0" />

:<math>\operatorname{E}[X^m] = \frac{1 - \kappa^2}{\prod_{n=0}^{m+1} [1-(2n-m-1) \kappa ]} \frac{m!}{\beta^m}</math>

where <math>f_\kappa(x)</math> is finite if <math>0 < m + 1 < 1/\kappa</math>.

The expectation is defined as:

:<math>\operatorname{E}[X] = \frac{1}{\beta} \frac{1 - \kappa^2}{1 - 4\kappa^2} </math>
and the variance is:
:<math>\operatorname{Var}[X] = \sigma_\kappa^2 = \frac{1}{\beta^2} \frac{2(1-4\kappa^2)^2 - (1 - \kappa^2)^2(1-9\kappa^2)}{(1-4\kappa^2)^2(1-9\kappa^2)} </math>

==== Kurtosis ====
The [[kurtosis]] of the ''κ''-exponential distribution of type I may be computed thought:

: <math>\operatorname{Kurt}[X] = \operatorname{E}\left[\frac{\left[ X - \frac{1}{\beta} \frac{1 - \kappa^2}{1 - 4\kappa^2}\right]^4}{\sigma_\kappa^4}\right] </math>
Thus, the [[kurtosis]] of the ''κ''-exponential distribution of type I distribution is given by:<blockquote><math>\operatorname{Kurt}[X] = \frac{ 9(1-\kappa^2)(1200\kappa^{14} - 6123\kappa^{12} + 562\kappa^{10} +1539 \kappa^8 - 544 \kappa^6 + 143 \kappa^4 -18\kappa^2 + 1  )}{ \beta^4 \sigma_\kappa^4 (1 - 4\kappa^2)^4 (3600\kappa^8 -4369\kappa^6 + 819\kappa^4 - 51\kappa^2 + 1) } \quad \text{for} \quad 0 \leq \kappa < 1/5  </math></blockquote>or<blockquote><math>\operatorname{Kurt}[X] = \frac{ 9(9\kappa^2-1)^2(\kappa^2-1)(1200\kappa^{14} - 6123\kappa^{12} + 562\kappa^{10} +1539 \kappa^8 - 544 \kappa^6 + 143 \kappa^4 -18\kappa^2 + 1  )}{ \beta^2 (1 - 4\kappa^2)^2(9\kappa^6 + 13\kappa^4 - 5\kappa^2 +1)(3600\kappa^8 -4369\kappa^6 + 819\kappa^4 - 51\kappa^2 + 1) } \quad \text{for} \quad 0 \leq \kappa < 1/5  </math></blockquote>The [[kurtosis]] of the ordinary [[exponential distribution]] is recovered in the limit <math>\kappa \rightarrow 0</math>.

==== Skewness ====
The [[skewness]] of the ''κ''-exponential distribution of type I may be computed thought:

: <math>\operatorname{Skew}[X] = \operatorname{E}\left[\frac{\left[ X - \frac{1}{\beta} \frac{1 - \kappa^2}{1 - 4\kappa^2}\right]^3}{\sigma_\kappa^3}\right] </math>
Thus, the [[skewness]] of the ''κ''-exponential distribution of type I distribution is given by:<blockquote><math>\operatorname{Shew}[X] = \frac{ 2 (1-\kappa^2) (144 \kappa^8+23 \kappa^6+27 \kappa^4-6 \kappa^2+1) }{ \beta^3 \sigma^3_\kappa (4 \kappa^2-1)^3 (144 \kappa^4-25 \kappa^2+1) } \quad \text{for} \quad 0 \leq \kappa < 1/4  </math></blockquote>The [[kurtosis]] of the ordinary [[exponential distribution]] is recovered in the limit <math>\kappa \rightarrow 0</math>.

== Type II ==

===Probability density function===
{{Probability distribution
  | name       = ''κ''-exponential distribution of type II
  | type       = density
  | parameters = <math> 0 \leq \kappa < 1 </math> [[shape parameter|shape]] ([[Real number|real]]) <br /> <math> \beta> 0 </math> [[rate parameter|rate]] ([[Real number|real]])
  | support    = <math>x \in [0, \infty)</math>
  | pdf        = <math> \frac{ \beta }{ \sqrt{1+ \kappa^2 \beta^2 x^2 } }
 \exp_\kappa(- \beta x) </math>
  | cdf        = <math>1-\exp_k({-\beta x)}</math>
  | mean       = <math>\frac{1}{\beta} \frac{1}{1 - \kappa^2}</math>
  | variance   = <math>\sigma_\kappa^2  = \frac{1}{\beta^2} \frac{1+2 \kappa^4}{(1-4\kappa^2)(1-\kappa^2)^2} </math>
  |pdf_image=File:Kaniadakis Exponential Distribution Type II pdf.png|cdf_image=File:Kaniadakis Exponential Distribution Type II cdf.png|mode=<math> \frac{ 1 }{ \kappa \beta \sqrt{ 2 (1 - \kappa^2) } } </math>|quantile=<math> \beta^{-1} \ln_\kappa \Bigg(\frac{1}{1 - F_\kappa} \Bigg) , 0 \leq F_\kappa \leq 1</math>|median=<math> \beta^{-1} \ln_\kappa (2) </math>|moments=<math> \frac{\beta^{-m} m!}{\prod_{n=0}^{m} [1-(2n- m) \kappa ]} </math>|kurtosis=<math> \frac{3 (72 \kappa^{10} - 360 \kappa^8 - 44 \kappa^6-32 \kappa^4+7 \kappa^2-3) }{ (4\kappa^2-1)^{-1} (2 \kappa^4+1)^2 (144 \kappa^4-25 \kappa^2+1) } </math>|skewness=<math> \frac{ 2 (15 \kappa^6+6 \kappa^4+2 \kappa^2+1) }{ (1 - 9\kappa^2)(2 \kappa^4 + 1) } \sqrt{ \frac{1 - 4\kappa^2 }{ 1 + 2\kappa^4 } } </math>}}

The Kaniadakis ''κ''-exponential distribution of Type II also is part of a class of [[statistical distributions]] emerging from the [[Kaniadakis statistics|Kaniadakis κ-statistics]] which exhibit power-law tails, but with different constraints. This distribution is a particular case of the [[Kaniadakis Weibull distribution|Kaniadakis ''κ''-Weibull distribution]] with <math>\alpha = 1</math> is:<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal |last=Kaniadakis |first=G. |date=2021-01-01 |title=New power-law tailed distributions emerging in κ-statistics (a) |url=https://iopscience.iop.org/article/10.1209/0295-5075/133/10002 |journal=Europhysics Letters |volume=133 |issue=1 |article-number=10002 |doi=10.1209/0295-5075/133/10002 |issn=0295-5075|arxiv=2203.01743 |bibcode=2021EL....13310002K |s2cid=234144356 }}</ref>

:<math> 
f_{_{\kappa}}(x) = 
\frac{\beta}{\sqrt{1+\kappa^2 \beta^2 x^2}}
\exp_\kappa(-\beta x)
</math>

valid for <math>x \ge 0</math>, where <math>0 \leq |\kappa| < 1</math> is the entropic index associated with the [[Kaniadakis statistics|Kaniadakis entropy]] and <math>\beta > 0</math> is known as [[rate parameter]]. 

The [[exponential distribution]] is recovered as <math>\kappa \rightarrow 0.</math>

===Cumulative distribution function===
The [[cumulative distribution function]] of ''κ''-exponential distribution of Type II is given by

:<math>F_\kappa(x) = 
1-\exp_k({-\beta x)}</math>

for <math>x \ge 0</math>. The cumulative [[exponential distribution]] is recovered in the classical limit <math>\kappa \rightarrow 0</math>.

=== Properties ===

==== Moments, expectation value and variance ====
The ''κ''-exponential distribution  of type II has moment of order <math>m < 1/\kappa</math> given by<ref name=":0" />

:<math>\operatorname{E}[X^m] = \frac{\beta^{-m} m!}{\prod_{n=0}^{m} [1-(2n- m) \kappa ]}</math>

The expectation value and the variance are:

:<math>\operatorname{E}[X] = \frac{1}{\beta} \frac{1}{1 - \kappa^2} </math>

:<math>\operatorname{Var}[X] = \sigma_\kappa^2 = \frac{1}{\beta^2} \frac{1+2 \kappa^4}{(1-4\kappa^2)(1-\kappa^2)^2} </math>

The mode is given by:

:<math>x_{\textrm{mode}} = \frac{1}{\kappa \beta\sqrt{2(1-\kappa^2)}} </math>

==== Kurtosis ====
The [[kurtosis]] of the ''κ''-exponential distribution of type II may be computed thought:

: <math>\operatorname{Kurt}[X] = \operatorname{E}\left[\left(\frac{X - \frac{1}{\beta} \frac{1}{1 - \kappa^2} }{\sigma_\kappa} \right)^4 \right] </math>

Thus, the [[kurtosis]] of the ''κ''-exponential distribution of type II distribution is given by:

:<math>\operatorname{Kurt}[X] = \frac{3 (72 \kappa^{10} - 360 \kappa^8 - 44 \kappa^6-32 \kappa^4+7 \kappa^2-3) }{ \beta^4  \sigma_\kappa^4 (\kappa^2 - 1)^4 (576 \kappa^6 - 244 \kappa^4 + 29 \kappa^2 - 1) } \quad \text{ for } \quad  0 \leq \kappa < 1/4  </math>

or

:<math>\operatorname{Kurt}[X] = \frac{3 (72 \kappa^{10} - 360 \kappa^8 - 44 \kappa^6-32 \kappa^4+7 \kappa^2-3) }{ (4\kappa^2-1)^{-1} (2 \kappa^4+1)^2 (144 \kappa^4-25 \kappa^2+1) } \quad \text{ for } \quad  0 \leq \kappa < 1/4  </math>

==== Skewness ====
The [[skewness]] of the ''κ''-exponential distribution of type II may be computed thought:

: <math>\operatorname{Skew}[X] = \operatorname{E}\left[\frac{\left[ X - \frac{1}{\beta} \frac{1}{1 - \kappa^2}\right]^3}{\sigma_\kappa^3}\right] </math>
Thus, the [[skewness]] of the ''κ''-exponential distribution of type II distribution is given by:<blockquote><math>\operatorname{Skew}[X] = -\frac{ 2 (15 \kappa^6+6 \kappa^4+2 \kappa^2+1) }{ \beta^3 \sigma_\kappa^3 (\kappa^2 - 1)^3 (36 \kappa^4 - 13 \kappa^2 + 1) } \quad \text{for} \quad 0 \leq \kappa < 1/3  </math></blockquote>or<blockquote><math>\operatorname{Skew}[X] = \frac{ 2 (15 \kappa^6+6 \kappa^4+2 \kappa^2+1) }{ (1 - 9\kappa^2)(2 \kappa^4 + 1) } \sqrt{ \frac{1 - 4\kappa^2 }{ 1 + 2\kappa^4 } } \quad \text{for} \quad 0 \leq \kappa < 1/3  </math></blockquote>The [[skewness]] of the ordinary [[exponential distribution]] is recovered in the limit <math>\kappa \rightarrow 0</math>.

==== Quantiles ====

The [[Quantile|quantiles]] are given by the following expression<blockquote><math>x_{\textrm{quantile}} (F_\kappa) = \beta^{-1} \ln_\kappa \Bigg(\frac{1}{1 - F_\kappa} \Bigg) </math></blockquote>with <math>0 \leq F_\kappa \leq 1</math>, in which the median is the case :<blockquote><math>x_{\textrm{median}} (F_\kappa) = \beta^{-1} \ln_\kappa (2) </math></blockquote>

==== Lorenz curve ====
The [[Lorenz curve]] associated with the ''κ''-exponential distribution of type II is given by:<ref name=":0" />

:<math>\mathcal{L}_\kappa(F_\kappa) = 1 + \frac{1 - \kappa}{2 \kappa}(1 - F_\kappa)^{1 + \kappa} - \frac{1 + \kappa}{2 \kappa}(1 - F_\kappa)^{1 - \kappa}</math>
The [[Gini coefficient]] is<blockquote><math>\operatorname{G}_\kappa = \frac{2 + \kappa^2}{4 - \kappa^2}</math></blockquote>

==== Asymptotic behavior ====
The ''κ''-exponential distribution of type II behaves [[asymptotically]] as follows:<ref name=":0" />

:<math>\lim_{x \to +\infty} f_\kappa (x) \sim \kappa^{-1} (2 \kappa \beta)^{-1/\kappa} x^{(-1 - \kappa)/\kappa}</math>
:<math>\lim_{x \to 0^+} f_\kappa (x) = \beta</math>

==Applications==
The ''κ''-exponential distribution has been applied in several areas, such as:
* In [[geomechanics]], for analyzing the properties of rock masses;<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Oreste |first1=Pierpaolo |last2=Spagnoli |first2=Giovanni |date=2018-04-03 |title=Statistical analysis of some main geomechanical formulations evaluated with the Kaniadakis exponential law |url=https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/17486025.2017.1373201 |journal=Geomechanics and Geoengineering |language=en |volume=13 |issue=2 |pages=139–145 |doi=10.1080/17486025.2017.1373201 |s2cid=133860553 |issn=1748-6025|url-access=subscription }}</ref>
* In quantum theory, in physical analysis using [[Planck's law|Planck's radiation law]];<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Ourabah |first1=Kamel |last2=Tribeche |first2=Mouloud |date=2014 |title=Planck radiation law and Einstein coefficients reexamined in Kaniadakis κ statistics |url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevE.89.062130 |journal=Physical Review E |language=en |volume=89 |issue=6 |article-number=062130 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevE.89.062130 |pmid=25019747 |bibcode=2014PhRvE..89f2130O |issn=1539-3755|url-access=subscription }}</ref>
* In [[Inverse problem|inverse problems]], the ''κ''-exponential distribution has been used to formulate a robust approach;<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=da Silva |first1=Sérgio Luiz E. F. |last2=dos Santos Lima |first2=Gustavo Z. |last3=Volpe |first3=Ernani V. |last4=de Araújo |first4=João M. |last5=Corso |first5=Gilberto |date=2021 |title=Robust approaches for inverse problems based on Tsallis and Kaniadakis generalised statistics |url=https://link.springer.com/10.1140/epjp/s13360-021-01521-w |journal=The European Physical Journal Plus |language=en |volume=136 |issue=5 |page=518 |doi=10.1140/epjp/s13360-021-01521-w |bibcode=2021EPJP..136..518D |s2cid=236575441 |issn=2190-5444|url-access=subscription }}</ref>
*In [[Network theory]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Macedo-Filho |first1=A. |last2=Moreira |first2=D.A. |last3=Silva |first3=R. |last4=da Silva |first4=Luciano R. |date=2013 |title=Maximum entropy principle for Kaniadakis statistics and networks |journal=Physics Letters A |language=en |volume=377 |issue=12 |pages=842–846 |doi=10.1016/j.physleta.2013.01.032|bibcode=2013PhLA..377..842M |doi-access=free }}</ref>
